idiom_name: typed message union + serialized queue (or XState actors)
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds the part JavaScript lacks - a message protocol you can check: model the mailbox as a queue of a discriminated union (type Msg = { type: 'add'; n: number } | { type: 'get'; reply: (n: number) => void }) and switch it exhaustively, so the compiler rejects unknown message shapes and forgotten cases; that is the typed analogue of Akka's Behavior[Msg]. The runtime structure stays the event loop's (private state plus one drain loop), and XState is the ready-made library form: createActor(logic) gives an actor with a mailbox that processes events one at a time, can invoke or spawn children and emits snapshots, as its actor-model page states. Choose the hand-rolled union for small in-process state, XState when lifecycle, spawning and visualization matter.
pitfalls: A discriminated union is only as good as its exhaustiveness: without a never-check in the default branch, a new message type compiles cleanly and silently does nothing at runtime.
The mailbox array is unbounded and the drain loop is synchronous, so a message burst blocks the event loop; bound the queue or yield between batches.
A reply callback that throws aborts the synchronous drain; catch or route callback failures through the actor's error policy so queued messages are not stranded.
Types are erased: the union protects the sender's compile time, not the runtime, so messages arriving from JSON, a worker or a socket still need runtime validation.
